name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz largely shut; tanker fires 5 Nov
summary: Hormuz largely shut; IRGC claims tanker fires on 5 Nov after mine claims on 4 Nov
state: The IRGC claimed on 5 Nov that two tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, a day after it said four tankers hit mines south of the strait; neither claim has been independently verified (The National; Gulf News). UKMTO reported two vessels attacked in Hormuz on 3 Nov (ABC News). Iran ties reopening the strait to an end to the US naval blockade, and an Iranian general warned of Red Sea attacks if the war resumes.
for_you: Shipping through the Gulf and Red Sea faces attack risk; follow UKMTO advisories and FCDO travel advice for the region.

sources.title: The National — Iran war latest: IRGC claims two tankers and tugboat caught fire in Strait of Hormuz

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
